ui.home.connect_title: To get started, connect your services.
ui.home.lede: PlaylistTransfer moves your music between {services}, in any direction. No new accounts: everything happens on your computer.
ui.history.title: History
ui.history.lede: Every transfer and every cleanup is recorded on your computer. Click one to see the details.
ui.history.empty_text: Your first one will show up here.
ui.history.empty_transfer: There are no transfers in the history.
ui.history.empty_dedupe: There are no duplicate cleanups in the history.

ui.transfer.lede: Choose from where and to where, the source playlist and one or more destinations.

ui.dedupe.title: Remove duplicates
ui.dedupe.lede: Finds the same song twice in a playlist, even in another version: another album, a remaster, mono or a video. The one that came first stays. Versions by other artists don't count as duplicates.
ui.dedupe.connect: Connect Tidal or YouTube Music to check your playlists.
ui.dedupe.versions_hint: Other versions (live, remix…) are left unchecked.
ui.dedupe.uncheck_hint: Uncheck the ones you want to keep.
ui.dedupe.confirm_text: The version that came first in the playlist stays. Removed songs are recorded in the history.

ui.history.download_title: A lightweight text file, to read or hand to an AI
ui.settings.sp_note: The app is yours and free: only you and up to 5 people you add in “User Management” can use it. Every 6 months Spotify asks you to connect again.
ui.dedupe.confirm_readd_one: {service} can't remove a single copy: it removes both and puts the one that stays back in its place. It will show as added today.
ui.dedupe.confirm_readd_other: {service} can't remove a single copy: for {n} songs it removes all copies and puts the one that stays back in its place. They will show as added today.
ui.home.title: Your playlists, on the service you want.
ui.home.f_transfer: Pick a playlist and the app looks for every song on the other service. Songs already there, even in another version, aren't added twice, and you decide the doubtful ones at the end.
ui.home.f_dedupe: Finds the same song twice, even if it's another video or a remaster. Nothing is removed until you confirm.
ui.home.f_history: Every transfer and every cleanup is saved, song by song.
ui.home.connect_text: Two are needed to move music; one to remove duplicates.
ui.settings.hint.spotify_setup: Needs Spotify Premium and your own app on Spotify: click “{button}” and follow the steps.
ui.settings.sp.premium: The Spotify account you'll create the app with must have Premium (Spotify requires it). If it doesn't, click “{button}”.
ui.settings.sp.open_form: Click “{button}”. Spotify's “Create app” page opens in your browser.
ui.settings.sp.open_form_btn: Open the form to create the app
ui.settings.sp.login: If Spotify asks you to log in, use the account that has Premium. If it asks you to accept its terms or verify your email, do it and click “{button}” again.
ui.settings.sp.app_name: In the “App name” field, paste this name:
ui.settings.sp.app_desc: In the “App description” field, paste this description:
ui.settings.sp.redirect: In the “Redirect URIs” field, paste this address and click the “Add” button to its right:
ui.settings.sp.redirect_note: If “This redirect URI is not secure” shows up in red below it, that's normal: go on to the next step.
ui.settings.sp.web_api: Under “Which API/SDKs are you planning to use?”, tick only the “Web API” box.
ui.settings.sp.terms: Tick the “I understand and agree with Spotify's Developer Terms of Service and Design Guidelines” box.
ui.settings.sp.save: Click “Save”. Spotify takes you to your app's page.
ui.settings.sp.settings: On your app's page, click “Settings”. If you closed that page, click “{button}” and open “PlaylistTransfer”.
ui.settings.sp.client_id: In the “Basic Information” tab, copy the “Client ID” value (32 letters and numbers). Don't copy the “Client secret”.
ui.settings.sp.paste: Paste the Client ID in this field and click “{button}”:
ui.settings.sp.agree: Spotify opens asking whether PlaylistTransfer may use your account: click “Agree” and come back to this window. When it's done, “Spotify ✓” shows up at the top.
ui.login.tidal.1: Click “{button}”: the Tidal page opens in {browser}. If you can't see it, look for {browser} in the taskbar.
ui.login.tidal.2: If Tidal asks you to log in, use your Tidal account. If you were already logged in, go on to the next step.
ui.login.tidal.3: Tidal asks whether you want to connect this device: accept.
ui.login.tidal.4: Come back to this window. When it's done, “Tidal ✓” shows up at the top.
ui.login.ytmusic.1: Click “{button}”: a new {browser} window opens, separate from yours and without your sessions. That's normal.
ui.login.ytmusic.2: In that window, sign in with the Google account you use on YouTube Music. If it doesn't ask next time, it's because the window remembers the session.
ui.login.ytmusic.3: When YouTube Music shows up, don't touch anything: the window closes by itself in a few seconds.
ui.login.ytmusic.4: Come back to this window. When it's done, “YouTube Music ✓” shows up at the top.
ui.login.ytmusic_firefox.1: Click “{button}”. If YouTube Music was already open in Firefox, that session is used and there's nothing else to do.
ui.login.ytmusic_firefox.2: If not, YouTube Music opened in Firefox: sign in with your Google account.
ui.login.ytmusic_firefox.3: Come back to this window. When it's done, “YouTube Music ✓” shows up at the top.
ui.login.spotify.1: Click “{button}”: Spotify opens in {browser}. If it asks you to log in, use your Spotify account.
ui.login.spotify.2: Spotify asks whether PlaylistTransfer may use your account: click “Agree”.
ui.login.spotify.3: Come back to this window. When it's done, “Spotify ✓” shows up at the top.
